tldr: Google added local-model support to the Antigravity SDK on Oct 14, letting agent workflows run on a developer's machine and mix in cloud models. DeepMind then used Antigravity for Science on antimicrobial peptide search.
whats_new: Google Cloud made Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 available inside Antigravity on Oct 20, extending it beyond Google's own models.
why_it_matters: Antigravity now spans local, Gemini and Claude models in one agent harness, so model routing can live in the harness instead of per-vendor tooling.

status.detail: Antigravity is widening from a Google-model agent tool to a multi-vendor, local-plus-cloud harness.

beats.headline: DeepMind applies Antigravity for Science to peptide discovery
Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 land in Antigravity

open_questions: Does Antigravity publish pricing or quota terms for the Claude models?
Can one agent run mix local and Claude models in a single workflow?
take_for_builders: If you evaluate agent harnesses, rerun your coding evals on Antigravity with Claude selected and compare against local-model runs for cost and code privacy.
